findings.source_passage: The dirt road we traveled on was now a mud pit fit for any hog. My cloak was soaked through and there were two puddles always with me, one in each of my riding boots.
findings.why_it_matters: The image 'two puddles always with me, one in each of my riding boots' is a voice-defining comic detail with a rhythm that marks the narrator's self-deprecating wit; the draft replaces it with 'each boot sloshed with its own private lake,' altering both the phrasing and the flat-comic register of the original.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore 'there were two puddles always with me, one in each of my riding boots' verbatim or very close; the specificity and rhythm are the joke.

findings.source_passage: I felt a little guilty at having dashed his hopes.
findings.source_locator: After Xander's 'Then I still must continue my dream' line
findings.why_it_matters: The source uses a plain, direct interiority sentence that establishes the narrator's self-awareness and empathy; the draft substitutes 'Guilt pricked me for squashing it,' which is tonally different (more literary-figurative) and misrepresents the narrator's flat, wry voice.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore the simpler, flatter phrasing 'I felt a little guilty at having dashed his hopes' to keep the narrator's register consistent.

findings.source_passage: I raised my head and saluted him. The raindrops nearly drowned me.
findings.source_locator: After 'I would not have you make the attempt again'
findings.why_it_matters: The two-sentence beat—physical action plus absurdist consequence—is a signature comic rhythm in this narrator's voice; the draft collapses it to 'I saluted, nearly drowning in raindrops,' losing the declarative punch of the separate sentence.
findings.suggested_fix: Split the salute and drowning consequence into two sentences as in the source to preserve the comedic timing.

findings.source_passage: Spiro leaned forward so I could see him as he shook his head.
findings.source_locator: During the bull-riding anecdote, Spiros's response
findings.why_it_matters: The source names 'Spiro' (dropping the 's'), a small character-voice quirk in the narration; the draft normalizes it to 'Spiros,' erasing a minor but distinctive textual oddity.
findings.suggested_fix: Minor; retain or note—not regeneration-level, but worth preserving the source's own spelling inconsistency as a voice marker.

findings.source_passage: I smiled, but the smile soon faded. Thinking about what I left behind reminded me of the rain. I huddled inside my wet cloak and shivered as the damp sank into my bones. The forest around us seemed so vast, and I felt like just a tiny, wet little speck in it.
findings.source_locator: After 'I would ask nothing else of you'
findings.why_it_matters: 'a tiny, wet little speck in it' is a quietly distinctive, self-diminishing image that ends the exchange on a specific emotional note; the draft's 'a tiny, shaking speck under the vast, dripping canopy' rephrases it with more florid language, softening the blunt plainness of the original.
findings.suggested_fix: Restore 'tiny, wet little speck in it' as close to verbatim as possible; the adjective chain 'tiny, wet little' is the voice signature.

summary: No high-severity signature losses; three medium-severity voice-flattening instances (the puddles-in-boots image, the 'dashed his hopes' interiority, and the salute beat) reflect mild but consistent tonal drift away from the narrator's flat comic register, and two low-severity findings round out the findings — insufficient individually or collectively to trigger regeneration.
